source:
Mira: The greenhouse tomatoes are splitting because we are watering on a fixed schedule. Three dry days then a flood, and the skins cannot keep up.
Olaf: They are splitting because the night temperature is dropping below twelve degrees. The skin stiffens in the cold and cracks when the fruit swells in the morning.
Mira: We have had cold nights every October and the splitting only started when the timer was installed.
Olaf: The timer was installed the same week the heater failed. You are looking at the wrong change.
Mira: Then fix the heater and keep the timer, and we will see which of us is right.
Olaf: Agreed, but fix the heater first so the test is clean.

extraction.mainQuestion: What is causing the greenhouse tomatoes to split?

positions.label: Irregular watering causes the splitting
positions.thesis: The tomatoes split because the timer waters on a fixed schedule that alternates dry spells with floods.
positions.steelman: Cold Octobers are routine, but the splitting began only when the timer arrived; the new variable is the watering pattern.

groundingQuotes.quote: The greenhouse tomatoes are splitting because we are watering on a fixed schedule.

positions.label: Cold nights cause the splitting
positions.thesis: The tomatoes split because night temperatures fall below twelve degrees after the heater failed, stiffening the skins.
positions.steelman: The heater failed the same week the timer went in, so the timing argument points equally at the cold; the mechanism of stiff skins cracking is well understood.

groundingQuotes.quote: They are splitting because the night temperature is dropping below twelve degrees.

claims.statement: The splitting began when the watering timer was installed, and cold Octobers preceded it without splitting.

resolution.condition: Repair the heater while keeping the timer and observe whether splitting continues.

groundingQuotes.quote: the splitting only started when the timer was installed
The timer was installed the same week the heater failed.

claims.statement: The heater failed the same week the timer was installed, so the onset of splitting cannot be attributed to the timer alone.

resolution.condition: Maintenance records for the heater and timer installation dates.

groundingQuotes.quote: You are looking at the wrong change.

commonGroundCandidates.statement: Fixing the heater while keeping the timer would test which explanation is right.

groundingQuotes.quote: Then fix the heater and keep the timer, and we will see which of us is right.
Agreed, but fix the heater first so the test is clean.

disagreementCandidates.question: Is the splitting caused by the watering pattern or by cold nights?
disagreementCandidates.summary: Both accept that the timer and the heater failure began the same week; Mira attributes the splitting to the watering pattern, Olaf to the cold.

participantStances.stance: The watering schedule; cold Octobers never split them before.
The cold; the heater failed the same week.

disagreementCandidates.resolutionCondition: Change one variable at a time and observe the fruit.

disagreementCandidates.question: Did the splitting begin with the timer, or with the heater failure in the same week?
disagreementCandidates.summary: Mira dates the onset to the timer; Olaf notes the heater failed the same week, so the onset does not single out either change.

participantStances.stance: The heater failed the same week; the onset is confounded.

disagreementCandidates.resolutionCondition: Compare the timer installation date, the heater failure date, and the first split fruit.
